newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malayan Banking raises lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Malayan Banking raises lending rate.

text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) said on Monday it is raising its base lending rate (BLR) to 9.35 percent from 9.10 percent effective July 15.

In a statement, Maybank said the last revision in its BLR -- the benchmark commercial loan rate banks offer their best clients -- was on January 4, 1997, when it was increased to 9.10 percent from 9.00 percent.

The rate boost by Malaysia's largest bank comes after a surge in interbank rates due to a tightening of liquidity in the banking system. Central Bank Negara has been intervening to protect the ringgit against speculative attacks in recent weeks.
On Monday, the overnight interbank rate was steady at 10 percent after trading as high as 15 percent earlier in the day.
The three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (Klibor) was fixed in the daily morning fixing at 14.9 percent from 11.15 on Friday.
The ringgit plunged to a 16-month low of 2.55 a dollar early on Monday, and was at 2.5435/45 to a dollar at around 0800 GMT.
